Risk statement: A staff or administrator account is compromised because MFA is optional, giving an attacker access to email, AWS, GitHub, or the Admin Panel and exposing patient data or disrupting service.
Treatment summary: MFA enforced for Google Workspace, AWS, GitHub, and the Admin Panel; phishing-resistant methods for administrators; insurance declaration corrected.

Risk statement: Former employees or contractors retain access to GitHub, AWS, or SaaS tools because offboarding is informal, allowing unauthorized code or data access.
Treatment summary: Offboarding checklist with HR-triggered deadline; leaver access removed before last working day; quarterly access reviews; former contractor accounts removed.

Risk statement: Backups cannot be restored after data corruption, ransomware, or a regional outage because restores are untested and there is no defined RPO, RTO, or DR plan, causing prolonged loss of patient records.
Treatment summary: RPO 1 hour and RTO 8 hours defined; cross-region backup copies; quarterly restore tests with evidence; DR plan exercised.

Risk statement: Support staff can view any patient record through the Admin Panel without view logging or least privilege, leading to unauthorized access, insider misuse, or undetected data exposure.
Treatment summary: Least-privilege support roles, time-bound record access, view and export audit logging, quarterly access reviews, and break-glass process.

Risk statement: The Pixelwave contract lacks confidentiality, security, audit, and data protection terms, so a contractor breach or misuse creates legal exposure and uncontrolled code access.
Treatment summary: Revised services agreement with NDA, security schedule, audit right, data protection terms, and access restrictions; contractor acknowledgement recorded.

Risk statement: A phishing email tricks an employee into disclosing credentials, leading to mailbox compromise, fraudulent customer communications, or onward phishing to clinics and patients.
Treatment summary: Quarterly awareness training, monthly phishing simulations, reporting button, DMARC reject policy, and strengthened email authentication.

Risk statement: A lost or stolen unencrypted laptop or desktop exposes patient or employee data because device inventory, encryption, and endpoint management are incomplete.
Treatment summary: Complete asset inventory, enforced full-disk encryption, MDM enrolment, remote wipe, and endpoint protection baselines.

Risk statement: An intrusion or malicious insider activity is not detected in time because logging retention is short and alerts are not reviewed, allowing data exfiltration to continue undetected.
Treatment summary: Central security log retention of 12 months, GuardDuty and CloudTrail alerts to an on-call channel, documented triage runbook, and weekly review.

Risk statement: An attacker exploits an unpatched application or infrastructure vulnerability because there is no vulnerability management or security testing, leading to platform compromise or outage.
Treatment summary: Continuous dependency and image scanning, patch SLAs by severity, annual penetration test, secure code review, and SAST in CI.

Risk statement: Shared credentials, shared SSH keys, and credentials stored in a Google Sheet allow unauthorized production access with no attribution.
Treatment summary: Company password manager, unique named accounts, IAM Identity Center, per-person SSH certificates, key rotation, and removal of shared credentials.

Risk statement: An incident is mishandled because there is no plan, severity scale, or notification process, causing a missed 72-hour contractual notification and regulatory breach.
Treatment summary: Incident response plan, severity matrix, on-call rota, notification templates, evidence handling, and two exercises per year.

Risk statement: Production patient data is copied unmasked into staging, so a staging compromise or broad engineer access exposes live health data.
Treatment summary: Automated masking pipeline for all staging refreshes, restricted staging access, synthetic data default, and verification evidence.

Risk statement: The ISMS is not credible or complete, causing certification failure, loss of three hospital tenders, and a failed Series B due diligence.
Treatment summary: Full ISMS documentation, risk-based treatment, internal audit, management review, and certification readiness assessment.

Risk statement: An unauthorized person enters the office or network cupboard and steals equipment or connects to the network because fobs, visitors, and physical areas are weakly controlled.
Treatment summary: Fob reconciliation, visitor escort and sign-in, locked network cupboard, clear desk checks, and CCTV coverage review.

Risk statement: A critical supplier suffers a breach or fails to meet its obligations, exposing patient data or disrupting service because there is no supplier register, due diligence, or DPA.
Treatment summary: Supplier register, tiered due diligence, DPAs and security terms, annual reviews, cloud assurance evidence, and exit plans.

Risk statement: Patient and customer data is retained indefinitely after contract termination because there is no retention schedule or deletion capability, breaching PDPL storage-limitation requirements.
Treatment summary: Retention schedule by data type, automated deletion jobs, legal hold process, and quarterly deletion evidence.

Risk statement: A contractor or personal device used for Nabd work is compromised, introducing malware or allowing data theft because it is unmanaged and outside endpoint controls.
Treatment summary: Contractor device minimum requirements, MDM for company email, remote working policy, and access limited to staging.

Risk statement: A faulty production change causes an outage during clinic hours because emergency changes bypass review and rollback is untested, damaging contractual availability and patient care.
Treatment summary: Change policy with emergency approval, protected branches without routine bypass, automated rollback tests, and post-implementation review.

Risk statement: The Admin Panel is reachable from the internet with password-only protection, allowing credential stuffing or exploitation that exposes all tenant data.
Treatment summary: Admin Panel restricted to VPN or IP allow-list, MFA enforced, WAF rate limiting, and separate administrative ingress.

Risk statement: Patient or employee data remains on laptops that are sold or reused because disposal is not controlled, causing a data leak after the device leaves Nabd.
Treatment summary: Certified wipe before disposal, disposal register, asset return checklist, and approved resale or recycling route.

Risk statement: Support staff paste patient details or screenshots into Freshdesk and Slack, causing unauthorized disclosure and uncontrolled copies of health data.
Treatment summary: Data handling rules for support, redaction guidance, DLP rules for email and chat, ticket templates, and quarterly quality checks.

Risk statement: Nabd processes patient data without a PDPL compliance programme, including an unassessed cross-border transfer to Bahrain, leading to regulatory enforcement or suspension of hosting.
Treatment summary: Records of processing, DPIA for the platform and transfer, data subject request procedure, DPO appointment, and supplier DPAs.

Risk statement: The platform falls below the contracted 99.9 percent availability because there is no capacity planning, load testing, or continuity capability, causing service credits and customer churn.
Treatment summary: SLO monitoring, capacity reviews, load testing before peak periods, multi-AZ verification, and DR invocation criteria.

Risk statement: A compromised dependency, CI/CD pipeline, or container image introduces malicious code into production because supply-chain controls are limited.
Treatment summary: Dependency pinning, automated scanning, signed images, OIDC instead of long-lived CI secrets, branch protection, and vendor review.

Risk statement: The DevOps Lead becomes unavailable and recovery or production change is blocked because AWS, CI/CD, and bastion knowledge sits with one person.
Treatment summary: Runbooks, cross-training for a second platform engineer, break-glass access, and documented recovery roles.

Risk statement: A patient account is taken over through OTP interception or SIM swap, exposing that patient's records and allowing fraudulent actions in their name.
Treatment summary: OTP rate limiting, device binding, session revocation, anomaly alerts, and patient notification guidance.
